q.young: How many times have you thrown up?
q.older: How many times have you vomited since you hit your head?

review.reason: chose yes/no phrasing (h-008) over a count; loses the CHALICE >=3 boundary, PECARN binary still backs it

q.young: Do you remember bumping your head?
q.older: Do you remember how it happened?

review.reason: merged: young tier kept, older tier taken from h-014 to match PECARN's definition

q.young: What were you doing when you hurt it?
q.older: What were you doing when you hurt your head?

review.reason: mechanism question is important; accepted pending a text or voice widget

q.young: Is your head hurting more than before?
q.older: Has your headache got worse since it happened?

review.reason: band-agnostic phrasing preferred over h-009

candidates.note: wording is timeframe-free; band widened to any so the trajectory item covers few-days/long-time per packet decision 5

q.young: Did everything go dark for a bit?
q.older: Did you lose consciousness?

review.reason: accepted at review

q.young: Does your head hurt really badly?
q.older: Is the pain severe?

review.reason: screen: severity adjectives

q.young: Is your head hurting more than before?
q.older: Is it worse than it was?

review.reason: screen: duplicate of h-004

q.young: Have you thrown up since you hurt your head?
q.older: Have you vomited since you hurt your head?

review.reason: vomiting as yes/no; reworded to be duration-band agnostic

q.young: Is it worse today than yesterday?
q.older: Is your headache worse today than yesterday?

review.reason: assumes a day has passed; breaks in the just-now band

q.young: Did your body become jerky afterwards?
q.older: Did any part of your body jerk or shake afterwards?

review.reason: kept with low confidence; flagged for clinical review - a child may not recall a seizure

q.young: Did you have a seizure?
q.older: Have you had a seizure since the injury?

review.reason: screen: names a seizure to the child

q.young: Has your head hurt for lots of days?
q.older: Has the headache lasted more than a week?

review.reason: redundant - the duration screen already captures how long it has hurt

q.young: Do you feel sleepy or slow?
q.older: Have you been unusually drowsy?

review.reason: child-reported sleepiness; traces to item 13, not the CHALICE criterion

q.young: Do you remember what happened?
q.older: Do you remember how it happened?

review.reason: merged into h-002

q.young: Have you thrown up and does your head hurt?
q.older: Have you vomited and is your head sore?

review.reason: compound question; redundant with h-008

q.young: Have you felt sick in your tummy?
q.older: Have you felt like you might throw up?

review.reason: nausea is distinct from vomiting; older tier rephrased, now traces to new item 14; older tier reworded 2026-09-06 — "might be sick" reads as "becoming ill" in US English and lost the nausea criterion

q.young: Since the moment when you hurt your head, have you been feeling sick at all?
q.older: Have you felt sick since the injury?

review.reason: redundant with h-008, and 15 words for the young tier

q.young: Does your head hurt now?
q.older: Is your head hurting at the moment?

review.reason: redundant - the intensity screen already captured head pain severity

q.young: If you fell down stairs, how many steps?
q.older: If you fell down stairs, how many steps did you fall?

candidates.why: Stairs are the one height a child can count, and CATCH's five-stair criterion is stated in steps rather than metres.
candidates.note: step count is the child-answerable proxy for CATCH's "5 stairs" threshold

review.reason: approved from the cold-run batch

q.young: Did a grown-up say you would not wake up?
q.older: Did anyone tell you that you were not awake or not answering for a moment?

candidates.why: Item 5 is partial and CHALICE requires it witnessed, so the question asks what the child was told rather than treating their own account as fact.
candidates.note: routes LOC through a witness, which is what CHALICE actually requires

review.reason: approved from the cold-run batch

q.young: Does your head hurt too much to play?
q.older: Is your headache stopping you doing things you would normally do?

candidates.why: A functional proxy for item 3 that avoids asking a child to rate a severity word; include only if the reviewer decides not to derive item 3 from the FPS-R screen.
candidates.note: functional interference instead of severity - satisfies decision 3

review.reason: approved from the cold-run batch

q.young: Is there a bit you cannot remember?
q.older: Is there a part of what happened that you cannot remember at all?

candidates.why: Catches amnesia the child has noticed themselves without using the banned blackout phrasing or asking for a duration.
candidates.note: closer to PECARN's 'inability to recall the entire event' than h-002

review.reason: approved from the cold-run batch

q.young: Did you fall off something? What was it?
q.older: If you fell, what did you fall from? For example the top bunk, a wall, or some stairs.

candidates.why: The three fall-height thresholds disagree, so the child names the object and the nurse maps it to whichever rule they use.
candidates.note: implements the fall-height decision with concrete examples

review.reason: two questions in one (fails the screen); item 6 is already served by h-003, which dedupes ahead of it, so nothing is lost

q.young: Was it hard to wake up this morning?
q.older: Was it harder than usual to wake up this morning?

candidates.why: A concrete moment the child can recall, which reports the same item 13 sleepiness without asking them to monitor their own drowsiness now.
candidates.note: asks something the MOODS "Tired" answer does not

review.reason: approved from the cold-run batch
